## History

The line of descent, oldest first:

- **the human proto-language**, 20 kyr ago: the reconstructed ancestor (human).
- **Isui (human 21, Ratal)**, 20 kyr ago: continued the proto-language in place (spoken by human).
- **Ruirey (halfling 29, Ratal)**, 1.5 kyr ago: formed when the speakers took up another language.

| | consonants | vowels | tones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the human proto-language, 20 kyr ago | 22: m n̪ n ŋ p b t d k ɡ ʔ ʔʲ ts dʒ s f v h ɻ j w ɾ | 10: i ĩ u e eː o õ ə ɛ ɔ | none |
| now | 17: m n̪ n ŋ p b d k ɡ ʔ s f ɹ ɻ j w l | 7: i u e o ə ʌ̞ a | none |

**Shift.** 1.5 kyr ago the halfling speakers of deme 646 took up the language of the human (human 21). Trigger: ?.
From the old language (halfling 29) 69 words were kept, mostly landscape, plants and animals: fish, dog, flower, leaf, louse, root, stone or rock, worm, bear, deer, grass, land, mountain, sea, ….
The accent the speakers brought (new sound heard as old): eː > e, iː > i, oː > o, t > p, ɛ > a, ɡ > k, ʐ > z.
Grammar carried over: adjective AN > NA; definite article post > none.

**Contact.** Sound changes taken up from neighbours by the wave along the line: halfling 6 (18), halfling 8 (15), human 21 (13), halfling 2 (6), human 21 (5), halfling 34 (5). Loan events in the present vocabulary (by donor): hill giant 3 (26), human 21 (16), human 86 (13), green dragon 9 (11), halfling 29 (9), silver dragon 2 (9).

## Phonology

### Consonants

| | Bilabial | Labiodental | Dental | Alveolar | Retroflex | Palatal | Labial-velar | Velar | Glottal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nasal** | m |  | n̪ | n |  |  |  | ŋ |  |
| **Plosive** | p · b |  |  | d |  |  |  | k · ɡ | ʔ |
| **Sibilant fricative** |  |  |  | s |  |  |  |  |  |
| **Non-sibilant fricative** |  | f |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| **Approximant** |  |  |  | ɹ | ɻ | j | w |  |  |
| **Lateral approximant** |  |  |  | l |  |  |  |  |  |

Where symbols share a cell, the voiceless ones come first and the voiced follow the dot. Secondary articulation (ʷ ʲ ˠ ˤ) and length (ː) stay in the cell of the plain sound.

### Vowels

| | Front | Central | Back |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Close** | i |  | u |
| **Close-mid** | e |  | o |
| **Mid** |  | ə |  |
| **Near-open** |  |  | ʌ̞ |
| **Open** | a |  |  |

Unrounded vowels come before the dot, rounded after it. Length: no long vowels. Nasality: no nasal vowels.

### Tone, syllables and stress

No phonemic tone.
Syllable shapes (share of syllables in the word-shape model): CV 33%, CVC 29%, CCV 13%, CCVC 10%, CVCC 6%, V 4%, VC 3%, CCVCC 2%. At most 2 consonant(s) before the vowel and 2 after it.
Stress falls on the first syllable.
Core words average 1.62 syllables (3.7 sounds); 28% of words share their form with another word.

### Allophony

| allophone | phoneme | where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [v] | /f/ | between vowels only |

## Orthography

The house romanization in two registers: the full spelling (workbench, one letter or digraph per sound, tone marks) and the book spelling (lossy: no tone, plain vowels, at most one diacritic letter a word).

**Consonants:** m ‹m› · n̪ ‹n̪› ‹n› · n ‹n› · ŋ ‹ng› · p ‹p› · b ‹b› · d ‹d› · k ‹k› · ɡ ‹g› · ʔ ‹'› · s ‹s› · f ‹f› · ɹ ‹ř› ‹r› · ɻ ‹ḻ› · j ‹y› · w ‹w› · l ‹l›

**Vowels:** i ‹i› · u ‹u› · e ‹e› · o ‹o› · ə ‹ë› ‹e› · ʌ̞ ‹e̞o› ‹eo› · a ‹a›

Where two spellings are given the second is the book spelling.

## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; noun before the numeral; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has a definite article after the noun, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, no alignment marking (subject and object are not told apart by form), singular and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past, future and perfective; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs agree with the subject by prefixes; not with the object.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; alienable and inalienable possession told apart; numeral classifiers; serial verbs; verb reduplication; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words left in place; a decimal counting base; locational possession ('at me is a dog').
Measured morphology: 14 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.9 (0 free word … 3 fused), 12 paradigm cells, 10 of them with allomorphy.
